result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cmty_girvan_newman()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Detect communities using an optimized Girvan-Newman algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L18352-L18440){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cmty_girvan_newman( attr_name=None, return_dict=False, most_valuable_edge=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Girvan-Newman communities](/assets/graphs/cmty-girvan-newman.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense clusters, a triangle A, B, C and a four-node cluster D, E, F, G, joined by the bridge C to D, drawn dashed because it has the highest betweenness and is cut first. It shares cmty_edge_btwns()'s implementation, so the result is identical: community 0 is A, B, C (accent) and community 1 is D, E, F, G (teal)." width="100%"} Iteratively removes the edge with highest betweenness centrality to reveal hierarchical community structure, returning the partition that maximizes Newman-Girvan modularity. Betweenness is recomputed only for the component that changed, with parallel BFS. `cmty_edge_btwns()` runs the same implementation and returns the same partition; this method also offers weighted betweenness via `most_valuable_edge="weight"`. When several edges tie for the highest betweenness, the one with the smallest endpoint IDs is removed first, so results are deterministic. (Other tools may break ties differently and so end up with a different, equally valid dendrogram.) Communities are numbered by their smallest node ID. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store community assignments in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `cmty_girvan_newman`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. [most_valuable_edge]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Strategy for selecting which edge to remove. If `"weight"`, uses edge weight in the betweenness calculation (Dijkstra instead of BFS). If `None` (default), treats the graph as unweighted. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to community IDs (0-indexed, contiguous). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is directed (requires undirected graph). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#6bf2b37e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), # Triangle 1 ("C", "D"), # Bridge edge ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) # Triangle 2 ) communities = graph.cmty_girvan_newman(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): cid for nid, cid in communities.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 0, 'B': 0, 'C': 0, 'D': 1, 'E': 1, 'F': 1} ``` ::: :::
